findings.claim: A jingle "is a specific type of sound creation".
findings.truth: The spec lists jingles at 4.1.1 as one of the ten forms of media. The six types of sound creation at 4.1.2 are Foley, ambience, dialogue, voice-overs, underscore and spot effects. The lesson's own key facts already list them correctly, so the sentence contradicts the rest of the lesson and could lead a student to write "jingle" when asked to name a type.

findings.claim: Flashcard 11: "Which video format is Apple's preferred uncompressed-style wrapper for editing?" - answer MOV.
findings.truth: MOV is a container, not an uncompressed format. It normally holds compressed video. The same lesson's key fact lists MOV under compressed formats and WAV and AIF as the only uncompressed ones, so the flashcard contradicts the lesson and could make a student answer "MOV" to "identify an uncompressed format".
findings.evidence: spec 4.1.5 format list (MP4, MOV, MP3, WAV, AIF); lesson 3 key fact n34

findings.claim: Six mark schemes (lessons 1, 2 and 3, questions 5 and 6) end their band ladder with "Lower band (1-2)".
findings.truth: House band vocabulary is Top band / Upper-mid band / Mid band / Lower-mid band / Low band. The bottom band must read "Low band". Lessons 1, 2 and 3 are all affected.

findings.claim: "The six DAW arrangement tools you must know are: video file import, audio/MIDI import, audio/MIDI editing, layering, automation, and markers."
findings.truth: The spec text at 4.1.4 extracts from a two-column PDF layout with four empty bullets and only three recovered words (layering, texture, impact). Layering therefore sits either in the DAW arrangement tools list or in the sound arrangement list. The lesson's reading is defensible and the other three words are taught correctly under sound arrangement, so no edit is made. Confirm against a clean copy of the spec PDF if one becomes available.

summary: Three lessons checked against the NCFE technical award spec for music technology (603/7008/7, v1.4 Nov 2025). No exam-structure errors: no lesson calls the qualification a GCSE, names a paper, a board, SPaG marks or an impossible tariff, and the practice tariffs (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8) sit inside the written examination's range. All fifteen knowledge-check keys and all three match orders recompute correct, and every mark scheme matches the corrected facts. Lesson 2 carries no factual error. Two content fixes: a jingle mislabelled as a type of sound creation, and a flashcard calling MOV an uncompressed format. One house-style fix across six mark schemes, and one note on the spec's column-extraction ambiguity.
